If the devotee makes any gift with anyone or anything in view, he shall have that everlasting benefit. His family shall be liberated from Piśāca-hood undoubtedly.

If the man takes the holy bath uttering anyone’s name that man (as named) becomes rid of Piśāca-hood. If anyone offers here pots or pitchers full of gruel, he attains permanent salvation. No Preta (ghost) is born in his family (i.e. none of his family will attain ghosthood). \[Tīrtha No. 2\]

By visiting Śiprāguṃpheśvara, a devotee of Rudra, who has conquered his sense-organs, is rid of all sins like a serpent getting rid of its slough. \[Tīrtha No. 3\]

A man of great devotion who takes the holy bath and visits Agastyeśvara shall leave off the abode of Yama and go to Rudraloka. \[Tīrtha No. 4\]

A man who bathes in Śiprā and visits Dhuṇḍheśvara Śiva, O Vyāsa, attains the benefit of a horse-sacrifice. There is no doubt about it. \[Tīrtha No. 5\]

Formerly, O Vyāsa, the Ḍamaru (hand-drum) was played upon by the Lord here. Hence the deity is known by the name Ḍamarukeśvara. There is no fear from ailment unto the man who devoutly visits Ḍamarukeśvara. On death he shall go to Śivapura. \[Tīrtha No. 6\]

The man who visits Anādikalpeśvara devoutly, obtains a kingdom like Lord Purandara (Indra) who got heaven. O Vyāsa, he is likely to be envied even by Devas always. He rejoices with all worldly pleasures for more than hundreds of crores of Kalpas. \[Tīrtha No. 7\]

He who visits Siddheśvara, Vīrabhadra and Caṇḍikā attains Siddhi here itself. The man obtains victory everywhere. \[Tīrtha Nos. 8, 9, 10\]

A devotee should take the holy bath in the Triviṣṭapa Tīrtha and visit Svarṇajāleśvara and worship the Lord with gold. He is liberated from all sins. \[Tīrtha No. 11\]

The man should take the bath and visit Karkoṭeśvara Śiva. He need not be afraid of serpents. He will never be indigent. He who visits the eternal Mahāmāyā with great devotion becomes rid of Visnumāyā and attains the greatest region. \[Tīrtha No. 12\]

The man who worships Kapāleśvara with great devotion shall be rid of great sins even if he is a Brāhmaṇa-slaughterer. \[Tīrtha No. 13\]

The man shall take the holy bath in Svargadvāra and visit Lord Bhairava. By visiting that Lord, one attains the benefit of a hundred Yajñas. \[Tīrtha No. 14\]

## Chapter 21 - The Greatness of Hanumatkeśvara

## \|\| 1.21.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*athānyatsaṃpravakṣyāmi devaṃ tridaśapūjitam \|*  
*hanumatkeśvaraṃnāma bhuktimuktiphalapradam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: Hanumān brought a Mauktika (pearl) Liṅga from Laṅkā and installed it near Rudrasaras in Avantī. Due to association with Hanumat the Liṅga became known as ‘Hanumatkeśvara’.

Sanatkumāra said:

1\. Henceforth I shall describe another deity, the Lord named Hanumatkeśvara who is adored by Devas and who bestows worldly pleasures and salvation as the benefit.

## \|\| 1.21.2 \|\|

*śaive sarasi yaḥ snātvā paśyeddhanumatkeśvaram \|*  
*kalpakoṭisahasrāṇi vāyuloke sa modate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He who takes the holy bath in Rudrasaras, the lake pertaining to Śiva, and sees Hanumatkeśvara, rejoices in Vāyuloka for thousands of crores of Kalpas.

## \|\| 1.21.3 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*hanumatkeśvaro yastu hyuktaḥ pūrvaṃ tvayā'nagha \|*  
*kathāṃ kathaya hyetasya vṛttapūrvāṃ sanātanīm \|\| 3 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

3\. O sinless one, narrate the story of Hanumatkeśvara, previously referred to by you, the ancient legend as it had happened.

## \|\| 1.21.4 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*trailokyakaṇṭakaḥ pūrvaṃ rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇunā rāmarūpeṇa laṃkāyāṃ vinipātitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:

4\. Formerly, the Rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa who was a thorn unto the three worlds, was slain and brought down in Laṅkā by Viṣṇu in the form of Rāma.

## \|\| 1.21.5 \|\|

*ghātayitvā tu taṃ duṣṭaṃ sītāmādāya jānakīm \|*  
*vānaraiḥ saha ṛkṣaiśca nagarīṃ svāmupāgataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. After killing that wicked one and taking Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, he reached his own city along with the monkeys and bears.

## \|\| 1.21.6-7 \|\|

*tatra rājyamanuprāpya ṛṣibhiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*kathāvasāne rāmeṇa hyagastyo munisattamaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*papraccha ca dvayorvīryaṃ śaṃbhuvātajayostadā \|*  
*tadā dāśarathiṃ prāha aga stirmunisattamaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. After regaining the kingdom Rāma seated amidst sages, asked Agastya, the excellent sage, at the end of the discourse, about the powers of the two—of Śaṃbhu and the son of Vāyu. Then Agasti, the excellent sage, said:

## \|\| 1.21.8 \|\|

*anaupamyo yathā devo yuddhe śauryaṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*jñeyo vāyusutastadvatsatyametadbravīmi te \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “Just as Lord Maheśvara is incomparable in regard to heroism in battle, so also the son of Vāyu should be known. I am speaking the truth.”

## \|\| 1.21.9-10 \|\|

*etacchutvātha hanumānyaddhareṇo pamā mama \|*  
*kṛtā munivareṇeha pratyakṣaṃ rāghavasya ha \|\| 9 \|\|*

*gamiṣye nagarīṃ laṃkāṃ liṃgamekaṃ prayācitum \|*  
*rākṣasendraṃ mahābhāgaṃ vibhīṣaṇamakalma ṣam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. On hearing this, Hanumān said (to himself), ‘Since my comparison has been made with Hara by the excellent sage in the presence of Rāghava, I shall go to Laṅkā (city) in order to request for a Liṅga from the blessed king of Rākṣasas, the sinless Vibhīṣaṇa.’

## \|\| 1.21.11 \|\|

*tato gataḥ sa laṃkāyāṃ vibhīṣaṇamuvāca ha \|*  
*dehi me tvaṃ mahābhāga liṃgamekaṃ ca śobhanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then he went to Laṅkā and requested Vibhīṣaṇa, “O blessed one, give me a splendid Liṅga.”

## \|\| 1.21.12-15 \|\|

*uktaṃ ca rākṣasendreṇa gṛhāṇaitadyathā ruci \|*  
*etāni ṣaṭ ca liṃgāni rāvaṇasthāpitāni vai \|\| 12 \|\|*

*trailokyavijayātpūrvaṃ mama bhrātrā mahātmanā \|*  
*eteṣu yadabhīṣṭaṃ te liṃgaṃ kathaya suvrata \|*  
*tatprayacchāmi te'dyaiva satyametatplavaṃgama \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tato jagrāha hanumāṃlliṃgaṃ mauktikasaṃnibham \|*  
*yadetaddṛśyate vīra tatprayaccha mamānagha \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śrutvā hanumato vākyamathovāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*dattametanmahāvīra liṃgaṃ yaddhṛtavānasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. The king of Rākṣasas said: “Take any Liṅga as you please. These six Liṅgas were installed by Rāvaṇa, my noble-souled brother, before the conquest of the three worlds. Tell me, O observer of holy Vratas, which Liṅga among these is desired by you? I shall give it to you. This is the truth, O monkey.”

## \|\| 1.21.14-18 \|\|

*tato jagrāha hanumāṃlliṃgaṃ mauktikasaṃnibham \|*  
*yadetaddṛśyate vīra tatprayaccha mamānagha \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śrutvā hanumato vākyamathovāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*dattametanmahāvīra liṃgaṃ yaddhṛtavānasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śrūyate hi purāvṛttaṃ liṃgametaddhaneśvaraḥ \|*  
*rudra bhaktyā samāyuktastrikālamapyapūjayat \|\| 16 \|\|*

*rāvaṇena yadā baddhastadānīṃ hi dhaneśvaraḥ \|*  
*liṃgasyāsya prabhāvena vimuktaḥ samapadyata \|\| 17 \|\|*

*prasādāttasya liṃgasya dhaneśo dhanarakṣakaḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā tanmahāliṃgaṃ svastho jāto'tha vānaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. Thereupon Hanumān took up a Liṅga shining like a pearl: “O sinless hero, give unto me this Liṅga that is seen (before you).” On hearing the words of Hanumān, Vibhīṣaṇa said: “O great warrior, the Liṅga that you are holding has already been given to you. It is reported that formerly Dhaneśvara (Kubera) endowed with devotion to Rudra, worshipped this Liṅga thrice a day. When he was taken a captive by Rāvaṇa, it was through the power of this Liṅga that Dhaneśvara became free. Due to the favour of that Liṅga Dhaneśvara could preserve his wealth.”

Taking away that great Liṅga, the monkey became happy and satisfied.

## \|\| 1.21.19 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*gṛhītvā tu tato liṃgaṃ prasthito vimaleṃ'bare \|*  
*saptame divase caiva saṃprāpto'vaṃtikāṃ purīm \|\| 19 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:

19\. Taking the Liṅga with him he (Hanumat) started his (flight) in the clear sky. On the seventh day he reached the city of Avantikā.

## \|\| 1.21.20 \|\|

*tatra rudrasarastīre sthāpya snānamathākarot \|*  
*mahākālasya pūjārthaṃ gamanaṃ pratyaciṃtayat \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Placing the Liṅga on the bank of Rudrasaras (lake), he took his bath. He was thinking of going to Mahākāla for the purpose of adoration.

## \|\| 1.21.21 \|\|

*uddhartukāmastalligamuddhartuṃ na śaśāka saḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He was desirous of lifting up that Liṅga. He could not lift it up.

## \|\| 1.21.22-23 \|\|

*tato vyavasthito devaḥ prāha taṃ vāyunandanam \|*  
*asminkṣetre hanūmanmāṃ tvannāmnaiva pratiṣṭhāpaya \|\| 22 \|\|*

*hanumatkeśvaraṃ cātha loke khyātaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*śailavacconnataṃ liṃgaṃ sthāpitaṃ vāyusūnunā \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. The Lord who had been installed thus told the son of Vāyu: “In this holy spot, O Hanumān, let this be installed in your own name. It shall be known all over the world as Hanumatkeśvara.” The Liṅga that is as high as a mountain has been installed by the son of Vāyu.

## \|\| 1.21.24-26 \|\|

*śanau paśyennaro yastu hanumatkeśvaraṃ śivam \|*  
*tasya śatrubhayaṃ nāsti saṃgrāme jayamāpnuyāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

*na ca caurabhayaṃ tasya na dāridryaṃ na durgatiḥ \|*  
*tailābhiṣekaṃ yaḥ kuryāddhanumatkeśvare śive \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tasya rogāḥ pralīyante grahapīḍā na jāyate \|*  
*ye drakṣyaṃti narāḥ bhaktyā teṣāṃ mokṣo bhaviṣyati \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. If a man visits Lord Śiva, Hanumatkeśvara, on Saturdays, he need not be afraid of enemies. He shall be victorious in war. He need not be afraid of thieves too. He has (i.e. suffers from) neither poverty nor ill-luck. If a devotee bathes Hanumatkeśvara Śiva with oil, all his ailments perish. He is not afflicted by malignant Planets. The man who visits with devotion this Liṅga becomes liberated.

## Chapter 22 - The Efficacy of Rudrasaras

## \|\| 1.22.1-3 \|\|

*\| śrīsanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*yameśvaraṃ tu yaḥ paśyetsnāpayitvā tilāṃbhasā \|*  
*kuṃkumena samālipya pūjayedutpalaistataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dahetkṛṣṇāgaruṃ dhūpaṃ dāpayettilataṇḍulān \|*  
*ya evamarcayeddevamīśvaraṃ śūlahastakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yatra kutra mṛtasyāpi yamaḥ pitṛsamo bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

Srī Sanatkumāra said:

1-3. Yameśvara should be bathed with water mixed with gingelly seeds. Then after smearing it with saffron, one should worship it with lilies.

Black agallochum should be burnt as incense, Gingelly seeds and raw rice-grains should be made over as religious gifts. He who visits Yameśvara thus and worships too the Lord armed with a trident will find Yama (as loving) as father, wherever he dies.

## \|\| 1.22.4 \|\|

*iti yameśvaramāhātmyam \|*  
*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*kathayāmi paraṃ vyāsa tīrthaṃ tīrtheṣu cottamam \|*  
*nāmnā rudrasaraḥ proktaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|\| 4 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:

4\. O Vyāsa, I shall describe another Tīrtha, the most excellent of all Tīrthas. It is known by the name Rudrasaras. It is well-known in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 1.22.5 \|\|

*tatra snātvā śucirbhūtvā paśyetkoṭeśvaraṃ śivam \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpebhyo rudralokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A devotee should take bath therein and be pure. He should then visit Koṭeśvara Śiva. He is rid of all sins. He goes to Rudraloka (the region of Rudra).

## \|\| 1.22.6-11 \|\|

*śrāddhaṃ tatraiva kṛtvā tu śṛṇu yatphalamāpnuyāt \|*  
*daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ vājapeyaśatasya ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*phalaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ vyāsa labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*pitṝnuddiśya yatkiṃcitkoṭitīrthe pradīyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*koṭitīrthe naraḥ snātvā dhyāyedyaḥ paramākṣaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

*mucyate sarvapāpebhyo nirmokena yathoragaḥ \|*  
*prātarutthāya yo vipra tatra snānaṃ karoti vai \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā devaṃ mahākālaṃ gosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*koṭitīrthe naraḥ snātvā saptarātroṣitaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*cāṃdrāyaṇasahasrasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|*  
*jāgaraṃ tatra kuryādyo hyanaṃtaphalamaśnute \|\| 11 \|\|*

6-11. Listen to the benefit he attains after performing Śrāddha there. There is no doubt in this, O Vyāsa, that he obtains ten million times the benefit of ten horse-sacrifices and of a hundred Vājapeyas. If anything is given in Koṭi Tīrtha with the Pitṛs in view, everything becomes ten million times more blessed. There is no doubt about this. The man who takes his holy bath in Koṭi Tīrtha and meditates upon the Supreme Absolute is liberated from all sins like a serpent released from its slough.

O Brāhmaṇa, he who gets up early in the morning and takes his holy bath there obtains the benefit of (the gift of) a thousand cows by seeing Lord Mahākāla. The man who takes bath in the Koṭi Tīrtha and stays there for seven nights absolutely pure, obtains the benefit of a thousand Cāndrāyaṇas. He who keeps awake at night enjoys infinite benefit.

## \|\| 1.22.12-15 \|\|

*gandhapuṣpārcanaṃ kṛtvā mahāsnapanapūrvakam \|*  
*ya evaṃ nayate rātriṃ sopavāso jiteṃdriyaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*labhate sarvakāmitvaṃ yatsurairapi durlabham \|*  
*kārtikyāmatha vaiśākhyāṃ devaṃ tatra prapūjayet \|\| 13 \|\|*

*gaṃdhapuṣpaiśca kālīnaistathā vastraiḥ suśobhanaiḥ \|*  
*karpūraṃ kuṃkumaṃ caiva śrīkhaṇḍamagaruṃ tathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*samabhāgāni kṛtvā tu śilāpṛṣṭhe ca peṣayet \|*  
*anulipya mahākālaṃ rudrasyānucaro bhavet \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. After Mahāsnāna (great bathing) the devotee should perform worship with scented flowers; he should spend the night fasting with the sense-organs controlled. He obtains Sarvakāmitva (‘fulfilment of all desires’) unobtainable even to Suras.

On the full-moon days in the months of Kārttika and Vaiśākha, the devotee should worship the Lord with fragrant flowers of the season, splendid clothes etc. Camphor, saffron, sandal and agallochum should be taken in equal quantities and powdered (pounded) on a rocky slab. Smearing Mahākāla with it, one becomes a servant of Rudra.

## Chapter 23 - Pilgrimage to Mahākāleśvara

## \|\| 1.23.1 \|\|

*\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*atha yātrāṃ pravakṣyāmi mahākālasya yatnataḥ \|*  
*śivāṃ śreyaskarīṃ puṇyāṃ puṇyalokapradāyinīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:

1\. Henceforth, I shall carefully describe the pilgrimage to Mahākāla. It is auspicious, meritorious and conducive to welfare. It bestows the meritorious worlds.

## \|\| 1.23.2 \|\|

*snātvā sarasi rudrasya dṛṣṭvā koṭeśvaraṃ śivam \|*  
*namaskṛtya tato gacchenmahākālaṃ sanātanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After taking the holy bath in Rudrasaras and visiting Koṭeśvara Śiva and bowing down to him, a devotee should proceed towards the eternal Mahākāla.

## \|\| 1.23.3 \|\|

*gandhaiḥ puṣpairnamaskāraiḥ saṃpūjya tridaśeśvaram \|*  
*praṇipatya tato gaccheddevaṃ kapālamocanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. After adoring the Lord of Devas by means of sweet scents, flowers and prostrations and bowing down to him, the devotee should go to Lord Kapālamocana.

## \|\| 1.23.4 \|\|

*tatraiva devadeveśaḥ kapālaṃ nyastavānkṣitau \|*  
*kapāle tatkṣaṇānnyaste tatrābhūlliṃgamuttamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It was exactly there that the Lord of the chiefs of Devas placed the Kapāla on the ground. No sooner was the Kapāla placed on the ground than the excellent Liṅga came up there.

## \|\| 1.23.5-6 \|\|

*kapālamocanaṃ nāma sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*tatra vai snapanaṃ kuryādājyapalaśatena vai \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tadardhārdhena pādena vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*kāle pūrṇe sa viprendra śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Indeed Kapālamocana is destructive of all sins. The deity should be bathed with a hundred Palas of ghee or half of that or even a quarter, without undue hesitation for expenses. O eminent Brāhmaṇa, when the time is fully ripe, he is honoured in Śivaloka.

## \|\| 1.23.7 \|\|

*namaskṛtya tato gacchetkapileśvaramuttamam \|*  
*darśanādasya devasya mucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After bowing down to him the devotee should proceed towards the excellent Kapileśvara. By visiting this Lord, he is liberated from the sin of killing Brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 1.23.8 \|\|

*hanumatkeśvaraṃ devaṃ tato gacchetsamāhitaḥ \|*  
*aiśvaryamatulaṃ vyāsa darśanādasya jāyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Thereafter, he should go with concentration and mental purity to Lord Hanumatkeśvara, O Vyāsa. By visiting this deity, one gets unparalleled Aiśvarya (affluence and lordship).

## \|\| 1.23.9 \|\|

*tato gacchenmahādevaṃ paippalākhyaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*yasya darśanamātreṇa muktiḥ syāddvijasattama \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then he should go to the great eternal Lord named Paippala, O excellent Brāhmaṇa, by the mere sight of that deity, there shall be salvation.

## \|\| 1.23.10 \|\|

*svapneśvaraṃ tato gacchedbhaktiśraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*darśanādasya devasya duḥsvapnaṃ ca vinaśyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thereafter he should go to Svapneśvara with faith and devotion. By visiting this Lord (the effect of) evil dream shall perish.

## \|\| 1.23.11 \|\|

*tato gacchenmahādevamīśānaṃ viśvatomukham \|*  
*yasya darśanamātreṇa viśvasyaiva patirbhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then he should go to the great Lord Īśāna Viśvatomukha (‘having faces all-round’). Merely by visiting this Lord, one shall be the Lord of the entire universe.

## \|\| 1.23.12 \|\|

*someśvaraṃ tato gacchejjitakrodho jiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭharogādidoṣebhyo darśanādasya mucyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thereafter, the devotee should go to Someśvara with anger fully restrained and the sense-organs properly controlled. By visiting this Lord he is liberated from the defects of leprosy etc.

## \|\| 1.23.13 \|\|

*vaiśvānareśvaraṃ vyāsa tato gacchetsamāhitaḥ \|*  
*tasya vṛddhiḥ sadā loke jāyate tasya darśanāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O Vyāsa, with great concentration and mental purity, he should go to Vaiśvānareśvara. Due to this visit, his prosperity always increases in the world.

## \|\| 1.23.14 \|\|

*bījapūrakahastaṃ tu laku līśaṃ tato vrajet \|*  
*rudratvaṃ darśanāttasya jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thereafter, the devotee should go to Lakulīśa with a pomegranate in his hand. There is no doubt about this, that identity with Rudra takes place by visiting that deity.

## \|\| 1.23.15 \|\|

*tato gacchenmahādevaṃ gadyāṇeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*yasya darśanamātreṇa jāyaṃte sarva siddhayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Thereafter, he should go to the great excellent Lord Gadyāṇeśvara. Merely due to the visit thereof all Siddhis are achieved.

## \|\| 1.23.16 \|\|

*abhyarthitaḥ sadā devaiḥ pūjitaḥ siddhikāraṇāt \|*  
*tenābhyarthiteśvaro'yaṃ vikhyāto vighnanāyakaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Since this deity is always requested and adored by Devas for the purpose of attainment of Siddhi, this deity Vighnanāyaka is well-known as Abhyarthiteśvara.

## \|\| 1.23.17 \|\|

*vayovṛddhaṃ tato gacchenmahākālaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*na rogo na jarāvyādhirdarśanānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Thereafter, the devotee should proceed towards Vayovṛddha (age-old) Mahākāla, the eternal deity. Due to his sight, ailments are prevented and old age checked. There is no doubt in this regard.

## \|\| 1.23.18 \|\|

*vighnanāśaṃ tato gacchetprāṇīśaṃ balamuttamam \|*  
*snānaṃ ghaṭaśataistasya kuryādbhaktyā samāhitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then he should go to Prāṇīśa, the excellent Bala (strength? or the brother of Kṛṣṇa), the destroyer of obstacles. He shall bathe the deity with hundreds of potfuls of water with devotion and concentration.

## \|\| 1.23.19 \|\|

*tasya caiva kṛte snāne labhyaṃte sarvasiddhayaḥ \|*  
*svargaścāpi sadā vyāsa darśanādasya jāyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. If the ablution is performed, all the Siddhis are obtained. Heaven too, O Vyāsa, is achieved through his sight.

## \|\| 1.23.20 \|\|

*tanayaṃ tamanūllaṃghya daṃḍa pāṇiṃ tato vrajet \|*  
*yasya darśanamātreṇa yamaloko na dṛśyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Without passing that son (of Lord Śiva), the devotee should go to Daṇḍapāṇi (‘Staff-armed’), the mere sight whereof makes Yamaloka disappear.

## \|\| 1.23.21 \|\|

*puṣpadantaṃ tato gacchedbhaktiśraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*yasya darśanamātreṇa mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then, with devotion and faith, he should go to Puṣpadanta. There, mere sight thereof enables one to be liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 1.23.22 \|\|

*guhyaṃ caiva mahākālaṃ tato gacchetsamāhitaḥ \|*  
*yasya darśanamātreṇa guhyapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then, with concentration and mental purity, he should go to Guhya Mahākāla, by the sight whereof he is rid of all secret sins.

## \|\| 1.23.23 \|\|

*tato gacchetsamādhistho durvāseśvaramuttamam \|*  
*yasya darśanamātreṇa kṛtakṛtyo naro bhavet \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With steadiness in meditation, he should thereafter go to the excellent Durvāseśvara, by the mere sight whereof a man becomes blessed and contented for having done his duties.

## \|\| 1.23.24 \|\|

*śvāsāvarodhanaṃ kṛtvā durvāsasaḥ samīpataḥ \|*  
*gaurīṃ gatvā mahādurgāṃ tyajecchvāsamanaṃtaram \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In the vicinity of Durvāsas, the devotee restrains his breath. After reaching Gaurī Mahādurgā, he should exhale (his breath).

## \|\| 1.23.25 \|\|

*tatrocchvāso vimoktyastāmabhyarcya tu sarvathā \|*  
*kāleśvaraṃ tato gaccheddevadevaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. There the breath should be let out after worshipping the goddess. Thereafter, he should go to Kāleśvara, Maheśvara, the Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.23.26-32 \|\|

*yasya darśanamātreṇa yamalokaṃ na paśyati \|*  
*vidhīśaṃ ca tato gaccheddevadevaṃ maheśvaram \|\| 26 \|\|*

*yasya darśanamātreṇa badhiratvaṃ na jāyate \|*  
*kīrtayedātmano nāma sthānaṃ gotraṃ ca tasya vai \|\| 27 \|\|*

*na kīrtayedyadā nāma sā yātrā viphalī bhavet \|*  
*devasyāgre tato vyāsa upaviśya samāhitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*bhaktiyuktastato brūyānnamaskṛtvā punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*mayā samarpitā yātrā tvatprasādānmaheśvara \|\| 29 \|\|*

*saṃsārasāgarāddhorānmāmuddhara jagatpate \|*  
*anena vidhinā yastu mahākālaṃ pradakṣayet \|\| 30 \|\|*

*pradakṣiṇīkṛtā tena saptadvīpā vasuṃdharā \|*  
*golakṣaṃ dvijalakṣāya dattvā yallabhate phalam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tatphalaṃ devadevasya sakṛddattvā pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*bhaktyā paramayā yukto mahākālaṃ pradakṣayet \|\| 32 \|\|*

26-32. By the mere sight thereof, he does not see (i.e. go to) Yamaloka.

Thereafter he should go to Vidhīśa Maheśvara, the Lord of Devas, the sight whereof removes deafness.

He shall proclaim his name, place of nativity and Gotra. If the name is not proclaimed that pilgrimage shall become futile. Thereafter, O Vyāsa, he should sit in front of the Lord with concentration and mental purity. He should bow down frequently with devotion and speak this: “O Maheśvara, due to your favour, my pilgrimage has been (concluded and) dedicated to you. O Lord of the universe, redeem me from the terrible ocean of worldly existence.” If the devotee circumambulates Mahākāla by this procedure; it is as beneficial as though the earth consisting of the seven continents has been circumambulated.

By circumambulating the Lord of Devas once, one gets the same fruit as is obtained by gifting a hundred thousand cows to a hundred thousand Brāhmaṇas. One shall circumambulate Mahākāla with the greatest devotion.

## \|\| 1.23.33-35 \|\|

*padepade yajñaphalamiti me śaṃkaro'bravīt \|*  
*ṣaṣṭikoṭi sahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭikoṭiśatāni ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*pūjitāni bhavaṃtyatra yātreśvarasamarcanāt \|*  
*ya evaṃ kurute yātrāṃ śivadhyānaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sahasradakṣiṇāṃ dadyāttasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*saptajanmakṛtātpāpānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. Śaṅkara has told me that at every step (in the Yātrā) he gets the benefit of a Yajña. By the worship of Yātreśvara here, it is as though sixty thousand crores and sixty hundred crores of deities have been worshipped.

Listen to the meritorious benefit of that devotee who performs Yātrā thus with due mental concentration on Śiva and makes monetary gifts of a thousand. He is rid of sins committed in the course of seven births.

## \|\| 1.23.36-41 \|\|

*evaṃ yātrāṃ samāpyātha gatvā nijagṛhaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*yātrādaivata saṃkhyānvai ṣaḍviṃśatidvijottamān \|\| 36 \|\|*

*bhojayecchivabhaktāṃśca śivadhyānaparāyaṇān \|*  
*savastrāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā prāpyānujñāṃ visarjayet \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yātrākrameṇa caikaikaṃ dvārāṃtaramanuvrajet \|*  
*dharmopadeśake paścātsarvopaskarasaṃyutām \|\| 38 \|\|*

*dhenuṃ payasvinīṃ dadyādvittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*bhuñjītātha svayaṃ vyāsa sarvabhṛtyasamanvitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*dīnānāthadaridrāṃdhavikalādyāṃśca bhojayet \|*  
*yadatra phalamuddiṣṭaṃ tadvadāmi śṛṇuṣva me \|\| 40 \|\|*

*kulānāṃ śatamuddhṛtya mātāpitroḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*kalpakoṭisahasrāṇi śivaloke sa modate \|\| 41 \|\|*

36-41. A man should thus conclude his pilgrimage and go home. He should feed twenty-six excellent Brāhmaṇas, that being the number of the deities visited in the course of the pilgrimage. He should also feed other devotees of Śiva, engrossed in the meditation of Śiva. He should make monetary gifts along with garments, get the formal permission and then send them off.

He should follow upto the doorway each one of them, in the order of the deities visited.

Afterwards he should give a milch cow with all appertunances to the preceptor of Dharma. He should not hesitate at all in spending money over this. Then, O Vyāsa, he should take food accompanied by all servants. He should feed the needy, the helpless, the poor, the blind, the handicapped etc. Listen to the benefit thereof which I shall mention.

He redeems a hundred generations of his mother and of his father and gains satisfaction. He rejoices in Śivaloka for thousands of crores of Kalpas.

## Chapter 24 - The Greatness of Vālmīkeśvara

## \|\| 1.24.1 \|\|

*\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*vālmīkeśvaramityākhyaṃ yastu devaṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*maunī dhyānaparo bhūtvā sa kavitvamavāpnuyāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: This Liṅga was installed by Vālmīki, a Brāhmaṇa-robber transformed into a sage-poet. This story is repeated in Skandapurāṇa, Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa (Vaiśākha Māhātmya chapter 21), Nāgarakhaṇḍa (chapter 124) and Pralhāsakhaṇḍa (chapter 298). The names of the robbers are Agniśarmā (in this chapter), Lohajaṅgha and Vaiśākha. These are credited with the authorship of Rāmāyaṇa.

Sanatkumāra said:

1\. He who worships the Lord named Vālmīkeśvara after meditating silently on him, shall attain the status of a poet.

## \|\| 1.24.2 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*kathamatra samutpannaḥ ko'sau vālmīkeśvaraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*yasya darśanamātreṇa kavitvamupajāyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

2\. Who is this Lord Vālmīkeśvara? What is the origin of such a Lord, the mere sight of whom bestows the power of composing poetry?

## \|\| 1.24.3 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*āsīdvyāsa purā vipraḥ sumatirbhṛgu vaṃśajaḥ \|*  
*rūpayauvanasaṃpannā tasya bhāryātha kauśikī \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:

3\. O Vyāsa, formerly there was a Brāhmaṇa named Sumati, born in the family of Bhṛgu. His wife Kauśikī was richly endowed with beauty and youth.

## \|\| 1.24.4 \|\|

*tasya putraḥ samutpanno hyagniśarmeti nāmataḥ \|*  
*sa pitrā procyamāno'pi vedābhyāsaṃ na manyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A son was born to him named Agniśarman. Though admonished by his father, he did not feel inclined towards the study of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.24.5 \|\|

*tato bahutithe kāle anāvṛṣṭirajāyata \|*  
*tasyāṃ vipadgataḥ so'tha dakṣiṇāmāśrito diśam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. After a lapse of many years there occurred a drought. Hence he, a victim of that disaster, went in the southern direction.

## \|\| 1.24.6 \|\|

*tato'sau sumatirvipraḥ sabhāryaḥ sa sutastathā \|*  
*videśaṃ kānanaṃ prāptaḥ kṛtvā cāśramamāśritaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then Brāhmaṇa Sumati accompanied by his wife and son reached a forest in an alien country. He built a hermitage and stayed there.

## \|\| 1.24.7 \|\|

*ābhīrairdasyubhiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃgo'bhūdagniśarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*āgacchati pathā tena yastaṃ haṃti sa pāpakṛt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Agniśarman came to be associated with Ābhīras and robbers. That sinner began to kill whoever came that way.

## \|\| 1.24.8-9 \|\|

*smṛtirnaṣṭā gatā vedā gataṃ gotraṃ gatā śrutiḥ \|*  
*kasmiṃścidatha kāle tu tīrthayātrā्prasaṃgataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*saptarṣayaḥ pathā tena suvratāḥ samupasthitāḥ \|*  
*agniśarmātha tāndṛṣṭvā hantukāmo'bravīdidam \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. His memory (of being a Brāhmaṇa) was lost and Vedas, Smṛtis, Gotra etc. all were forgotten.

On a certain occasion, the Seven Sages of great holy vows came that way in the course of their pilgrimage. On seeing them, Agniśarman desired to kill them. He said thus:

## \|\| 1.24.10 \|\|

*vastrāṇīmāni mucyadhvaṃ chatrikopānahau tathā \|*  
*hantavyā hi mayā yūyaṃ gantāro yama sādane \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “Give up these clothes, slippers and umbrellas. You all will be killed by me. You will go to the abode of Yama.”

## \|\| 1.24.11 \|\|

*tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā atrirvacanamabravīt \|*  
*asmatpīḍanajaṃ pāpaṃ kathaṃ te hṛdi vartate \|*  
*vayaṃ tapasvino bhūtvā tīrthayātrākṛtodyamāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On hearing his words, Atri spoke these words: “How can you think of committing the sin of torturing us. We being ascetics, are engaged in pilgrimage.”

## \|\| 1.24.12 \|\|

*agniśarmovāca \|*  
*mamāsti mātātha pitā suto bhāryā garīyasī \|*  
*poṣayāmi sadā tāṃstu etanme hṛdi saṃsthitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

Agniśarman said:

12\. This is what I keep in my mind: I have a mother, a father, a son and a wife all important ones to me. I have to make provision for their food.

## \|\| 1.24.13-16 \|\|

*atriruvāca \|*  
*pitrādīnāśu pṛcchasva svakarmopārjitaṃ prati \|*  
*yadyuṣmadarthaṃ kriyate pāpaṃ tatkasya kathyatām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yadi te kathayaṃti sma mā mṛṣā prāṇino vadhīḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*agniśarmovāca \|*  
*na kadācinmayā te tu saṃpṛṣṭā īdṛśaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*yuṣmākaṃ vacasā me'dya pratibodhaḥ pravartate \|\| 15 \|\|*

*gatvā pṛcchāmi tānsarvānkasya bhāvaśca kīdṛśaḥ \|*  
*yūyamatraiva tiṣṭhadhvaṃ yāvadāgamanaṃ mama \|\| 16 \|\|*

Atri said:

13-16. Immediately ask your father and others regarding what you earn through your (sinful) activities: “Whose is that sin which is being committed for your sake?” It is possible that they may say, “Do not kill living beings in vain.”

## \|\| 1.24.17-20 \|\|

*ityuktvā tāñjagāmāśu pitaraṃ svamuvāca ha \|*  
*dharmasya pratighātena prāṇināṃ pīḍanena ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sumahaddṛśyate pāpaṃ kasya tatkathyatāṃ mama \|*  
*pitā prāha tathā mātā nāpuṇyamāvayoriha \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tvaṃ jānāsi yatkuruṣe kṛtaṃ bhāvyaṃ punastvayā \|*  
*tayostadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhāryā vacanamabravīt \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tayāpyuktaṃ na me pāpaṃ pāpametattavaiva hi \|*  
*tadvākyamabravītputraṃ bālo'hamitiso'bravīt \|\| 20 \|\|*

Agniśarman said:

Never before have they been asked like this (by me). It is due to your speech that sense has dawned on me. I shall go and ask all of them: “Who thinks and feels how?” All of you do wait here till I come back.

17-19a. After telling them this, he went to his father and asked, “A great sin is seen being committed by disregarding Dharma and injuring living beings. Whose is that sin of mine? May it be told.” The father and mother said, “The sin is not ours. You know what you commit. Hence what is done should be thought over (experienced) by you.”

19b-20. On hearing the words of the two, the wife spoke these words: “It is not my sin. All the sin is yours.”

He said the same words to his son and the son said, “I am only a boy.”

## \|\| 1.24.21-22 \|\|

*tajjñātvā hṛdayaṃ teṣāṃ ceṣṭitaṃ caiva tattvataḥ \|*  
*naṣṭo'hamiti manvānaḥ śaraṇaṃ me tapasvinaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kṣiptvātha laguḍaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ yena vai jaṃtavo hatāḥ \|*  
*prakīrya keśāṃstvarita ṛṣīṇāmagrataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. On realizing their feelings in the heart of hearts and their reaction too in the light of the fact, he felt thus, “I am doomed. The sages alone are my refuge.”

Then he cast off his black stick wherewith many creatures had been killed. Keeping his hairs dishevelled, he immediately went and stood before the sages.

## \|\| 1.24.23-24 \|\|

*praṇamya daṃḍapātena tato vacanamavravīt \|*  
*na me mātā na ca pitā na bhāryā na ca me sutaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sarvaistaiḥ parimuktau'haṃ bhavatāṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*suṣṭhūpadeśadānānmāṃ narakāttrātumarhatha \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. He prostrated before them like a log of wood and spoke these words: “I have no mother or father. I have neither a wife nor a son. I have been abandoned by all of them. Hence I am seeking refuge in you. It behoves you to save me from hell by offering excellent instructions and words of advice.”

## \|\| 1.24.25-27 \|\|

*evaṃ taṃ vādinaṃ dṛṣṭvā ṛṣayo'trimathābruvan \|*  
*bhavato vacanādasya pratibodhaḥ samāgataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*bhavatā'yamanugrāhyaḥ śiṣyo bhavatu te mune \|*  
*tathetyuktātha tānprāha cāgniṃ dhyānaṃ samācara \|\| 26 \|\|*

*anena dhyānayogena mahāmaṃtrajapena ca \|*  
*anekadustarātyugrapāpakṛjjanaghātakaḥ \|*  
*saṃsthito vṛkṣa mūle tvaṃ parā siddhiṃ gamiṣyasi \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. On hearing him speak thus, the sages said to Atri, “By your words sense has dawned on him. He should be favoured by you. O sage, let him be your disciple.” After saying to them, “Let it be so,” he (Atri) said to Agni (i.e. Agniśarman): “Practise meditation. By this practice of Dhyāna and the repetition of a great Mantra (i.e. name of Rāma), seated at the root of the tree you will attain the great Siddhi, although you have been a slayer of people and perpetrator of many terrible crimes and sins very difficult to subdue.”

## \|\| 1.24.28 \|\|

*ityuktvā te yayuḥ sarve saṃkāmaṃ so'pi tatra vai \|*  
*taddhyānastho'bhavadyogī vatsarāṇi trayodaśa \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After saying thus, all of them went away as they pleased. He (Agni) became a Yogin remaining in the state of meditation for thirteen years.

## \|\| 1.24.29-31 \|\|

*tasyoparyabhavattatra valmīko'vicalasya ca \|*  
*nivṛttāstu pathā tena munayastatra śuśruvuḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*udīritaṃ dhvaniṃ tena valmīke vismayānvitāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ khanitvā valmīkaṃ kāṣṭhībhūtoruśaṃkubhiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*taṃ dṛṣṭvotthāpayāmāsurmunayo nayasaṃyutam \|*  
*namaścakre'tha tānsarvānsa vipro munipuṃgavān \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. As he remained motionless, an anthill grew over him. On returning by that path, the sages heard someone speaking in the anthill. They were surprised at it. With spikes fitted to logs of wood, they dug up the anthill. On seeing him the sages tactfully (skilfully) lifted him up. That Brāhmaṇa (Agni) bowed down to those eminent sages.

## \|\| 1.24.32-34 \|\|

*tānprāha praṇato bhūtvā tapasā dīptatejasaḥ \|*  
*prasādādbhavatāmadya jñānaṃ labdhaṃ mayā śubham \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dīno'hamuddhṛtaḥ sarvairmagno'haṃ pāpakardame \|*  
*tasyeti te vākyamūcuḥ paramadhārmikāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*valmīke'sminsthitaḥ putra yatastvamekacittataḥ \|*  
*vālmīkiriti te nāma bhuvi khyātaṃ bhavi ṣyati \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-33a. With his radiance born of penance, he bowed down humbly and said: “Due to your favour, auspicious knowledge has been acquired by me now. Wretched as I was, I have been redeemed by all of you. I had sunk deep into the mire of sins.”

33b-34. On hearing these words of his, those excessively pious sages spoke these words: “O son, since you stayed within the Valmīka (anthill) with perfect concentration, your name Vālmīki will become well-known all over the earth.”

## \|\| 1.24.35-37 \|\|

*ityuktvā munayo jagmuḥ svāṃ diśāṃ tapasānvitāḥ \|*  
*gateṣu munimukhyeṣu vālmīkistapatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*kuśasthalyāmathāgamya samārādhya maheśvaram \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tasmātkavitvamāsādya cakre kāvyaṃ manoramam \|*  
*rāmāyaṇaṃ ca yatprāhuḥ kathāṃ suprathamasthitām \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tataḥ prabhṛti deveśo vālmīkeśvarasaṃjñakaḥ \|*  
*khyāto'vaṃtyāṃ tato vyāsa nṛṇāṃ kavitvadāyakaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. After saying this, the sages endowed with penance, went in the direction of their own (choice). When the eminent sages had gone, Vālmīki, the most excellent one among performers of penance, went to Kuśasthalī and propitiated Maheśvara and composed a pleasing epic poem, which they call Rāmāyaṇa. It is the first among narrative poems.

Ever since then the Lord of Devas named Vālmīkeśvara became well-known in Avantī bestowing poetic ability on men.

## \|\| 1.24.38 \|\|

*iti te kathitaṃ liṃgaṃ vālmīkeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*yasya darśanamātre ṇa kavitvamupapadyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thus the excellent Liṅga, Vālmīkeśvara has been described to you. Merely by visiting that Lord, ability to compose poems comes up naturally.

## Chapter 25 - The Greatness of Śukreśvara and Other Shrines

## \|\| 1.25.1 \|\|

*\| sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*śukreśvaraṃ samabhyarcya sitapuṣpairvilepanaiḥ \|*  
*praṇipatya tato bhaktyā rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:

1\. By worshipping Śukreśvara with white flowers and unguents and prostrating thereafter with devotion, (a devotee) is honoured in Rudraloka.

## \|\| 1.25.2 \|\|

*bhīmeśvaraṃ naro dṛṣṭvā bhaktyā saṃpūjya yatnataḥ \|*  
*na bhayaṃ labhate vyāsa raṇe rātrau jale'nale \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. By visiting Bhīmeśvara and worshipping him carefully and devoutly, O Vyāsa, a devotee does not face fears arising from battle, water, fire and nights.

## \|\| 1.25.3 \|\|

*gargeśvaraṃ snāpayitvā tilatailena mānavaḥ \|*  
*bilvapatraistu saṃpūjya dharmavṛddhimavāpnuyāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. By bathing Gargeśvara with gingelly oil and by worshipping with Bilva leaves, a man attains increase in piety.

## \|\| 1.25.4 \|\|

*upoṣitaścaturdaśyāṃ tilaprasthatilāṃbhasā \|*  
*snāpayitvā tilairiṣṭvā sadā saukhyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The devotee should observe fast on the fourteenth lunar day. He should bathe (the Lord) with water mixed with gingelly seeds measuring a Prastha. He should then perform Homa with gingelly seeds. Thereby he shall always attain happiness.

## \|\| 1.25.5 \|\|

*gosahasraṃ naro dattvā bhāvaṃ kṛtvā viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*bhavabaṃdhavinirmukto rudralokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. By offering the gift of a thousand cows with special emotional fervour, the devotee shall be rid of the bondage of the world. He goes to Rudraloka (region of Rudra).

## \|\| 1.25.6 \|\|

*kāmeśvaraṃ samabhyarcya kuṃkumādivilepanaiḥ \|*  
*kāmikena vimānena yāti svargaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. By worshipping Kāmeśvara with unguents of saffron etc. the devotee undoubtedly goes to heaven by means of an aerial chariot that can go wherever one pleases.

## \|\| 1.25.7 \|\|

*cūḍāmaṇiṃ namaskṛtya navamyāṃ kārtike site \|*  
*na viyoniṃ naro yāti dharmabuddhiḥ sa jāyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. By bowing down to Cūḍāmaṇi on the ninth day in the bright half of Kārttika, a man averts the danger of ignominious birth. He becomes pious-minded.

## \|\| 1.25.8 \|\|

*caṃḍīśvaraṃ samabhyarcya kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāmupoṣitaḥ \|*  
*nirmālyollaṃghanotthena na śokenāpi lipyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The devotee, should observe fast and worship Caṇḍīśvara on the eighth lunar day in the dark half. He is not touched by grief arising from passing over Nirmālya (the remnants of adoration).

## \|\| 1.25.9 \|\|

*ityāditīrthāni maheśvarasya puṇyāni sarvāṇi naro'bhigamya \|*  
*viśuddhacitto bhuvi bhāvitātmā prayāti śaṃbhorbhuvanaṃ suramyam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A man should proceed to all these meritorious and holy Tīrthas of Maheśvara. He should keep his mind pure and his soul pious. He goes to the world of Śaṃbhu which is very beautiful.

## Chapter 26 - The Glory of Mandākinī-Kṣetra

## \|\| 1.26.1 \|\|

*\| vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*guhyasthāne pavitrāṇi kīrtitāni tvayā mune \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ kathayasvādya mahākālavanasya me \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyasa said:

1\. O sage, sacred shrines in Guhya Sthāna have been described by you. Now tell me the dimensions and extent of Mahākālavana.

## \|\| 1.26.2 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*yathāśrutaṃ mayā pūrvaṃ gadato brahmaṇaḥ svayam \|*  
*tatte'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi śṛṇu tvaṃ gadato mama \|\| 2 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:

2\. I shall tell you as was heard by me formerly when Brahmā himself was saying. Listen to me as I say it.

## \|\| 1.26.3-4 \|\|

*yojanasyaiva paryaṃtaṃ caturdikṣūpaśobhitam \|*  
*sauvarṇaistoraṇaiścaiva muktādāmavilaṃbibhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dvārāṇi tatra śobhaṃte kāṃcanaiḥ kalaśaiḥ sthitaiḥ \|*  
*sitapadmamukhairdvārairanekamaṇimaṃḍitaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Upto the extent of a Yojana, it shines splendidly in the four quarters by means of golden ornamental gates and arches from where pearl-strings are suspended. There are golden waterpots with white lotuses on their tops (mouths). And the gates are adorned with a number of precious stones.

Pañceśānī Yātrā:

## \|\| 1.26.5 \|\|

*maheśvaraprayuktāśca dvārādhyakṣā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*dvāreṣu teṣu śobhaṃte lokānugrahakārakāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. At the portals, powerful doorkeepers employed by Maheśvara shine splendidly. They render great favour unto all the worlds.

## \|\| 1.26.6 \|\|

*piṃgaleśaḥ sthitaḥ pūrve bālarūpo vibhāvasuḥ \|*  
*tīrthasyābhimukho gauro gururgaṇairathānugaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Piṅgaleśa, in the form of a boy, is stationed in the east. He is (brilliant) like fire. Fair-complexioned and majestic, he stands facing the Tīrtha followed by Gaṇas.

## \|\| 1.26.7-16 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe'pi mahāyogī kāyāvarohaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*vitteśaḥ paścime dvāre kṣetrasyābhimukhaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*niyukto vai maheśena vāruṇīṃ diśamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*uttarāṃ diśamāśritya sthitaścaivottareśvaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sādhakaḥ sarvakāryāṇāmādiṣṭaḥ śaṃkareṇa saḥ \|*  
*mānavā ye vasaṃtyatra kṣetramadhye sudhārmikāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mṛtā rudrapuraṃ yāṃti vimānaiḥ sārvakāmikaiḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāmatha vārkendusaṃgame \|\| 10 \|\|*

*paṃceśānīṃ namaskṛtya pratilomānu lomataḥ \|*  
*upoṣito dinaikena dhyāyamāno maheśvaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

*mucyate sarvapāpaistu bahujanmakṛtairapi \|*  
*evaṃ ca vipra yo yātrāṃ paṃceśānīṃ samārabhet \|\| 12 \|\|*

*anenaiva svadehena rudralokaṃ sa gacchati \|*  
*paṃceśānīmathānyāṃ te sukhena kriyate yathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tathā śṛṇu pravakṣyāmi sarvapāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*prātaḥ snātvā rudrasarasyekādaśyāṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā mahākālaṃ natvā ceśānamīśvaram \|*  
*piṃgaleśaṃ tataḥ prāpya snātvā śrāddhaṃ samācaret \|\| 15 \|\|*

*upagamya tato devaṃ gaṇeśaṃ piṃgaleśvaram \|*  
*gandhaiḥ puṣpaiśca dhūpaiśca tamabhyarcya nivartayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

7-13a. The great Yogin, Kāyāvarohaṇeśvara (Nakulīśa) is stationed in the south. In the west, facing the holy spot, is stationed Bilveśa. Appointed by Maheśa, he has occupied the western quarter.

Uttareśvara stands stationed resorting to the northern direction. He has been ordered by Śaṅkara to accomplish all tasks. Righteous men who stay here in this holy spot, go to Rudrapura on death by means of aerial chariots going everywhere as desired.

The devotee should bow down to Pañceśānī (‘the group of five Iśāna deities’) either on the fourteenth day in the dark half or on the new-moon day when the Sun and the Moon come together. They can be bowed to in the due order or in the reverse order. He should observe fast for a day meditating upon Maheśvara. He is liberated from all the sins committed in the course of many births.

O Brāhmaṇa, thus the devotee who begins the pilgrimage of Pañceśānī goes to Rudraloka with this body of his.

13b-16. I shall explain to you another Pañceśānī Yātrā to facilitate its smooth performance. Listen. It is destructive of all sins.

The devotee takes his holy bath early in the morning on the eleventh day (of the lunar month) with great mental concentration and purity. After the performance of Śrāddha, he bows down to Mahākāla, Īśāna, Īśvara. Thereafter he should go to Piṅgaleśa for taking his holy bath and perform Śrāddha. Then he approaches Lord Gaṇeśa Piṅgaleśvara. After worshipping the deity with scents, incense and flowers, he should return.

## \|\| 1.26.17 \|\|

*mahākāleśvaraṃ prāpya bhūyaḥ snāto jiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*arcayeddevadeveśaṃ svayaṃbhuvaṃ sanātanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Again he goes to Mahākāla and takes his holy bath. With the sense-organs under control, he adores the self-born eternal Lord of the chiefs of Devas.

## \|\| 1.26.18 \|\|

*īśāne gamayedrātriṃ kṛtvā vai naktabhojanam \|*  
*dhyāyamāno maheśānaṃ bhūmau vinyasya vigraham \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He should spend the night at Iśāna after dinner. Meditating on Maheśāna, he should lie down on the ground.

## \|\| 1.26.19 \|\|

*dvādaśyāṃ pūrvavatsarvaṃ prātaḥ snātvā vrajennaraḥ \|*  
*kāyāvarohaṇaṃ gatvā piṃgaleśvaravadyajet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On the twelfth day, the man takes his morning bath as before and goes to Kāyāvarohaṇa, where he offers worship as per procedure as in the case of Piṅgaleśvara.

## \|\| 1.26.20 \|\|

*trayodaśyāmathāpyevaṃ bilveśaṃ paścime'rcayet \|*  
*caturdaśyāṃ tathā saumye pūjayeduttareśvaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On the thirteenth day, he should worship in the same manner Bilveśa in the west. So also on the fourteenth day, he should worship Uttareśvara in the north.

## \|\| 1.26.21 \|\|

*amāvāsyāṃ śuciḥ snāto mahākāleśvaraṃ yajet \|*  
*gandhaiḥ puṣpaiśca dhūpaiśca naivedyairvividhaistathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On the new-moon day, he should take his holy bath. Thus becoming clean he should worship Mahākāleśvara with scents, incense and flowers as well as food-offerings (Naivedyas) of diverse kinds.

## \|\| 1.26.22 \|\|

*gītanṛtyādikaṃ kṛtvā praṇipatya kṣamāpayet \|*  
*yātrāṃ kṛtvā tu pūrvoktāṃ tato nijagṛhaṃ vrajet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. After the performance of music, dances, etc., he should bow down and crave pardon (for omissions and commissions). After performing the pilgrimage as mentioned before, he should go home.

## \|\| 1.26.23-26 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānbhojayetpañca śivabhaktiparāyaṇān \|*  
*praṇamya devatārūpānmahākāloṣitāndvijān \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pūjayitvā hiraṇyena sūkṣmavastraguṇairnavaiḥ \|*  
*rathaṃ piṃgalake dadyādgajaṃ kāyāvarohaṇe \|\| 24 \|\|*

*dattvā bilveśvare cāśvaṃ vṛṣaṃ dattvā tu cottare \|*  
*dhenuṃ dattvā mahākāle sarvopaskarasaṃyutam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ya evaṃ kurute vyāsa tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. He should feed five Brāhmaṇas devoutly attached to Śiva. Then he should bow down to the Brāhmaṇas, the residents of Mahākāla deemed to be the deity himself. He should adore and propitiate them with gold and fresh clothes of nice texture. The gift to be made at Piṅgalaka is a chariot, that at Kāyāvarohaṇa is an elephant, a horse at Bilveśvara and a bull at Uttareśvara. The gift at Mahākāla is a cow. Everywhere the usual appertenances should be given too. Listen to the benefit and merit of the person who does like this, O Vyāsa.

## \|\| 1.26.27 \|\|

*pitṛkairmātṛkaiḥ sārdhaṃ kulaiḥ sa divi modate \|*  
*apsarogītanṛtyādyairvimānaiḥ sārvakāmikaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He rejoices in heaven along with all the members of his mother’s and father’s families accompanied by dance and music etc. of the celestial damsels and also aerial chariots that can go wherever one pleases. Here ends the greatness of the Yātrā of Pañceśānī.

Seven Names of Avantī

## \|\| 1.26.28 \|\|

*iti paṃceśānīyātrāmāhātmyam \|*  
*yastu pradakṣiṇāṃ kuryānniyamena kuśasthalīm \|*  
*pradakṣiṇīkṛtā tena saptadvīpā vasundharā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If anyone regularly circumambulates Kuśasthalī, it is (as beneficial as though) the entire earth consisting of the seven continents has been circumambulated.

## \|\| 1.26.29 \|\|

*yastu padmāvatīṃ paśyeddarcayetpaṃkajairnaraḥ \|*  
*dattvā dhūpaṃ sanaivedyaṃ mṛto brahmapuraṃ vrajet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The man who visits Padmāvatī and adores her with lotuses, offering incense along with Naivedya, shall go to Brahmapura on death.

## \|\| 1.26.30 \|\|

*svarṇaśṛṃgāṭikāṃ vyāsa kusumaiḥ svarṇasaṃnibhaiḥ \|*  
*samabhyarcya mahābhaktyā sa yāti śivamandiram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. O Vyāsa, by worshipping Svarṇaśṛṅgāṭikā with flowers resembling gold with great devotion, he goes to Śiva’s palace.

## \|\| 1.26.31 \|\|

*avantinīṃ tu yaḥ paśyeddevīṃ trailokyaviśrutām \|*  
*kāmikena vimānena yāti pauraṃdaraṃ puram \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He who visits Goddess Avantinī well-known all over the three worlds, goes to the city of Purandara by means of an aerial chariot able to go anywhere as one chooses.

## \|\| 1.26.32 \|\|

*arcayetpaṃkajairbhaktyā yo devīmamarāvatīm \|*  
*amaraiḥ saha saṃhṛṣṭo modate divi sarvadā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He who devoutly worships Goddess Amarāvatī with lotuses, becomes highly delighted and always rejoices in heaven with the immortal ones.

## \|\| 1.26.33 \|\|

*devīmujjayanīṃ bhaktyā yaḥ paśyati samāhitaḥ \|*  
*sarvaiśvaryasamāyukto rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. He who visits Goddess Ujjayanī with devotion, mental concentration and purity, becomes honoured in Rudraloka richly endowed with all amenities of affluence.

## \|\| 1.26.34 \|\|

*viśālāṃ caiva yaḥ paśyedrudrabhaktyā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*mucyate trividhaiḥ pāpairnātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He who has become pure due to the devotion to Rudra and visits Viśālā becomes rid of the three types of sins. No doubt need be felt here.

Thus Ends the Greatness of Sri Kalpasaptaka (‘Seven names of Avantī in seven Kalpas’).

## \|\| 1.26.35 \|\|

*iti śrīkalpasaptakamahimā \|*  
*śṛṇu vyāsa mahātīrthaṃ purā yadbrahmaṇārcitam \|*  
*akūreśvaramityākhyaṃ yatra siddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Listen, O Vyāsa, to the description of the great Tīrtha formerly adored by Brahmā. It is named Akrūreśvara and there Pitāmaha became a Siddha.

## \|\| 1.26.36 \|\|

*tatra devārcanaṃ kṛtvā kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāmupoṣitaḥ \|*  
*jiteṃdriyaḥ śucirdāṃto rudralokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. A person should worship the deity there after observing fast on the eighth lunar day in the dark half, with sense-organs conquered, mind subdued and body kept clean. He shall attain Rudraloka.

## \|\| 1.26.37 \|\|

*na vadetkenacitsārdhaṃ naraḥ prātargṛhe sthitaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā'krūreśvaraṃ devaṃ hemadānaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. While staying in the house in the morning the man should not speak to anyone. By visiting Lord Akrūreśvara he shall attain the fruit of the gift of gold.

Thus ends the Greatness of Akrūreśvara

## \|\| 1.26.38 \|\|

*ityakrūreśvaramāhātmyam \|*  
*yastu paśyati brahmāṇaṃ śuciḥ snāto jiteṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*mucyate pātakāddhorādbrahmalokaṃ mṛto vrajet \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The devotee should take the holy bath, keep himself clean and control his sense-organs and visit Brahmā. He is liberated from terrible sins. On death, he goes to Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 1.26.39 \|\|

*padmāsanasthito brahmā dhyāyamānaḥ paraṃ padam \|*  
*vasiṣṭhādyairmunivarairvijñaptaḥ karmasaṃbhavān \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Brahmā seated himself in Padmāsana posture meditating on the highest state. He was approached with a request by Vasiṣṭha and other sages regarding Karmas and Saṃbhava (birth).

## \|\| 1.26.40 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*ādityā marutaḥ sādhyāstathā caivāśvināvubhau \|*  
*pitaro ye ca lokānāṃ pūjyaṃte bhuvi mānavaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

The Sages said:

40\. Ādityas, Maruts, Sādhyas, two Aśvins, and Pitṛs of the worlds—all these are worshipped on the earth by human beings.

## \|\| 1.26.41 \|\|

*grahārkatārakā yakṣā diggajāścyānalānilāḥ \|*  
*amī devā vayaṃ sarve tvadaṃśāḥ paripaṭhyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. It is said (in scripture) that planets, sun, stars, Yakṣas, Diggajas, fire, wind and all of us, Devas, are parts of yours.

## \|\| 1.26.42 \|\|

*kathaṃ dhyāyasi deveśa etatsarvaṃ bravīhi naḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Tell us how do you meditate, O Lord of Devas?

## \|\| 1.26.43 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*dve vidye tattvarūpe ye parā caivāparā tathā \|*  
*te dve ca mama rūpe dve nitye mūrtātmike mama \|\| 43 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

43\. There are essentially two Vidyās. They are Parā and Aparā, Both of them are eternal and corporeal. They are my forms.

## \|\| 1.26.44 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*pitāmaha kathaṃ vidmo bhavaṃtaṃ paramaṃ vibhum \|*  
*yenāsmākaṃ parā siddhirjāyate tava darśanāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

The Sages said:

44\. O Pitāmaha, how shall (can) we know you, the greatest Lord, whereby the greatest Siddhi can be achieved at your sight?

## \|\| 1.26.45-47 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*māheśvaraṃ paraṃ kṣetraṃ kuśasthalīti śabditam \|*  
*yajñārthinā mayā devaḥ śrīkaṃṭhaḥ pārvatī patiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*yācitastena devena ukto'haṃ parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*samaṃtādyojanaṃ sāgraṃ kṣetrametatpitāmahaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*mayā dattaṃ tava vibho mahākālavanādṛte \|*  
*vāritaḥ sa mayā tatra vane gupto hi roṣataḥ \|*  
*kapardinā ca tatrokto yāsyāmo na tavāṃtikam \|\| 47 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

45-47. The holy spot called Kuśasthalī is very great. It was requested for by me who was desirous of performing a Yajña. Lord Śrīkaṇṭha, the consort of Pārvatī, was requested. I was told by that Lord Parameṣṭhin: “O Pitāmaha, this holy spot extending to more than a Yojana all-round has been given to you except the Mahākālavana.” Though restrained I remained hidden there in the forest. I was told angrily by Kapardin (Śiva), “We shall not come near you.”

## \|\| 1.26.48 \|\|

*ārabdho vai tato yajño nārāyaṇaparigrahāt \|*  
*jñātastathāpi me yajño devadevena śaṃbhunā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Thereupon the Yajña was begun by taking (the help of) Nārāyaṇa. Still my Yajña came to be known by Śaṃbhu, the Lord of Devas.

## \|\| 1.26.49 \|\|

*yajñavāṭaṃ kapardīśastato bhikṣārthamāgataḥ \|*  
*yājñikaiḥ so'tha tatrokto mātra tiṣṭha jugupsitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Lord Kapardin came to the Yajñavāṭa (enclosure of Yajña) for the sake of alms. He was told there by the Yajña priests, “Do not stand here, you despicable one.”

## \|\| 1.26.50-51 \|\|

*kapardinā ca te tatra uktā yāsyāmyahaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*evamuktvā kapālaṃ sa bhūmau saṃsthāpya tatra hi \|\| 50 \|\|*

*snātuṃ nadīṃ yayau śiprāṃ kapardī parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*uktaṃ tasmingate śiprāṃ kapardini dvijātibhiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Those persons there were told by Kapardin, “Then I shall come again.” After saying this he placed the skull on the ground. The great Lord Kapardin went to river Śiprā for bathing. After Kapardin had gone to Śiprā, the Brāhmaṇa said:

## \|\| 1.26.52-53 \|\|

*kathaṃ hi kriyate homaḥ kapāle sadasi sthite \|*  
*akapālāni śaucāni purā proktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*tatkapālaṃ sadasyena ukṣiptaṃ pāṇinā svayam \|*  
*tasminkṣipte'bhavaccānyatpunaḥ kṣipte'bhavatpunaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. “How is the Homa to be performed? The Kapāla is in the sacrificial hall. Learned men of yore have said that purity is spoilt by skulls (Kapāla).”

The Kapāla (skull) was lifted up by the Sadasya (member priest) himself with his hand. When it was lifted another Kapāla occupied its place. When that was removed another came up.

## \|\| 1.26.54 \|\|

*evaṃ nāṃtaṃ kapālānāṃ prāpyate munisattamāḥ \|*  
*rudraṃ kapardinaṃ matvā śaraṇaṃ taṃ samāgatāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Those excellent sages could not see the end of these Kapālas. Thinking that the Kapardin (‘man with matted hairs’) was Rudra, they sought refuge in him.

## \|\| 1.26.55 \|\|

*tataḥ sa darśanaṃ prādādbhaktyā tuṣṭo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*kapālapāṇirbhagavānmāmuvā ca tataḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thereupon Maheśvara who was pleased with their devotion made himself visible. The Lord with Kapāla in his hand said to me:

## \|\| 1.26.56-57 \|\|

*varaṃ varaya bho brahmanyatte manasi vartate \|*  
*nāstyadeyaṃ mayā tubhyaṃ sarvaṃ dāsyāmi tattvataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*brahmottaramidaṃ sthānaṃ mayā dattaṃ caturmukha \|*  
*kārayasva yathākāmaṃ yathāvarṇacatuṣṭayam \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. “O Brahmā, choose a boon, whatever may be in your mind. There is nothing which cannot be granted to you. I shall actually give you everything. O Four-faced One, this place called Brahmottara has been given. Get everything done as you please in regard to the four castes.”

## \|\| 1.26.58 \|\|

*evaṃ vadaṃtaṃ varadamīśānaṃ parameśvaram \|*  
*tatheti coktvā sadasi na mayā'nyo varo vṛtaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. I said, “So be it” to Īśāna Parameśvara who said thus in the open assembly. No other boon was chosen by me.

## \|\| 1.26.59 \|\|

*ujjayinīti vai nāma kuśasthalyā niveśitam \|*  
*kuṃḍaṃ maṃdākinī tatra mayā kṛtamanaṃtaram \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The name Ujjayinī was given to Kuśasthalī. Thereafter the holy pit called Mandākinī was made there by me.

## \|\| 1.26.60-63 \|\|

*tatra viprāḥ kṛte snāne sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*tasyāṃ saṃsthāpayeddikṣu caturo'rthaghaṭāñchubhān \|\| 60 \|\|*

*satilāstānsavastrāṃśca saphalānmaṃḍakaiḥ saha \|*  
*kārtikyāmatha māghyāṃ ca cātu rvidye pradāpayet \|\| 61 \|\|*

*prathamaṃ ca ṛgvedāya yajurvedāya dakṣiṇam \|*  
*paścimaṃ sāmavedāya atharvaṇe tathottaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

*vedānuddiśya cāpyevaṃ prīyatāṃ me pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*kṛte caivaṃ hi yatpuṇyaṃ tacchṛṇudhvaṃ samāhitāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

60-63. O Brāhmaṇas, if the holy bath is taken there, one is liberated from all sins. The devotee should place four auspicious Arthaghaṭas (waterpots of specific purpose) in the four quarters filled with gingelly seeds and wrapped in clothes along with fruits and baked cakes in the festival days in the month of Kārttika or Māgha. They are to be given to scholars of the four Vedas. The first (eastern) one (is to be given) to Ṛgveda, the southern one to Yajurveda, the western one to Sāmaveda and the northern one to Atharvan. He should utter this Mantra: “This has been gifted with the Vedas in view; thus may Pitāmaha be pleased.” Listen attentively to the merit, if this is done.

## \|\| 1.26.64 \|\|

*sarvatīrtheṣu yatpuṇyaṃ maṃdākinyāṃ tathā bhavet \|*  
*sahasraguṇitaṃ snānaṃ jāpyaṃ lakṣaguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The benefit derived from all other Tīrthas becomes increased thousand-fold in the case of holy bath and hundred thousand in the case of Japas.

## \|\| 1.26.65 \|\|

*dānaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ jñeyaṃ maṃdākinyāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kaumude māsi saṃprāpte godānaṃ tatra kārayet \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The gift should be known as increased ten million times in Mandākinī undoubtedly. In the month of Kaumuda (i.e. Kārttika), the devotee should make the gift of a cow.

## \|\| 1.26.66 \|\|

*ghṛtadhenuṃ ca kārtikyāṃ māghyāṃ tilamayīṃ tathā \|*  
*jaladhenuṃ tu vaiśākhyāṃ dattvā mucyeta pātakaiḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. In the month of Kārttika, Ghṛta Dhenu (cow made of ghee) should be gifted; in the month of Māgha that of gingelly seeds, of Jaladhenu in Vaiśākha (or the articles referred to are gifted along with a cow). Thereby the devotee shall be rid of sins.

## \|\| 1.26.67 \|\|

*vācikaṃ mānasaṃ pāpaṃ karmajaṃ yacca duṣkṛ tam \|*  
*vinaśyetkilbiṣaṃ sarvaṃ maṃdākinyāstu darśanāt \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. By the sight of Mandākinī all sins, verbal, mental and physical, perish.

## \|\| 1.26.68 \|\|

*maṃdākinīsamaṃ tīrthaṃ pṛthivyāṃ naiva dṛśyate \|*  
*yasya darśanamātreṇa brahmaloke sa modate \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. A Tīrtha on a par with Mandākinī is not seen on the earth. The devotee rejoices in Brahmaloka merely by seeing it.

## \|\| 1.26.69 \|\|

*maṃdākinyāṃ tu yaḥ snānaṃ kṛtvā śrāddhaṃ pradāsyati \|*  
*darśe ca pūrṇimāyāṃ vā pitṛloke sa modate \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. One who takes the holy bath in Mandākinī and performs Śrāddha on the full-moon day and on the new-moon day rejoices in the world of Pitṛs.

## \|\| 1.26.70-72 \|\|

*pitāmahaṃ tu yo bhaktyā nityaṃ paśyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*aśvamedhasahasreṇa rājasūyaśatena ca \|\| 70 \|\|*

*yujyate nātra saṃdehaḥ satyametattapodhanāḥ \|*  
*tato manvaṃtare'tīte prāpte vaivasvate punaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tenaivonmattaveṣeṇa ūrdhvaśeṣo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*praviṣṭo brahmaṇaḥ satre dṛṣṭastairdvija sattamaiḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

70-72. A man who sees Pitāmaha everyday, becomes united with (i.e. gets) the benefit of a thousand horse-sacrifices and a hundred Rājasūyas. There is no doubt in this, O ascetics. This is the truth. After the Manvantara came to a close and Vaivasvata Manvantara arrived again, Maheśvara entered the sacrificial hall of Brahmā with the same guise of an insane person with erected penis.

## \|\| 1.26.73 \|\|

*te brāhmaṇāḥ śapaṃti sma nindāṃ kurvaṃti cāpare \|*  
*apare pāṃśubhiḥ śiśnaṃ ghnaṃti tasyāśapandvijāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Those Brāhmaṇas began to curse; others censured him. Still others struck the penis with dust. The Brāhmaṇas cursed his (activity).

## \|\| 1.26.74 \|\|

*loṣṭhairlaguḍakaiścā nye ghnaṃti taṃ balagarvitāḥ \|*  
*jaṭāmukuṭakaṃ keciddhṛtvā karṣaṃti cāpare \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Others, haughty with power hit him with lumps of clay and sticks. Others caught hold of his crown-like matted hairs and pulled him.

## \|\| 1.26.75-80 \|\|

*pṛcchaṃti bratacaryāṃ vai kena vrataṃ ca darśitam \|*  
*atra caiva striyaḥ saṃti kathametattvayā kṛtam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*brahmaṇā cedṛśī caryā viṣṇunā vā kṛtā svayam \|*  
*giriśenāpi devena kenedaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*mā viḍambaya deveśaṃ vadhyo hi nastvamadya vai \|*  
*evaṃ tairhanyamānastu brāhmaṇaistatra śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*smitaṃ kṛtvā'bravītsarvānbrāhmaṇānparameśvaraḥ \|*  
*kiṃ yūyaṃ māmabhi hatha hyunmattaṃ naṣṭacetasam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*yūyaṃ kāruṇikāḥ sarve maitrabhāve vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*tamevaṃ vādinaṃ devaṃ jālmarūpadharaṃ haram \|\| 79 \|\|*

*māyayā tasya devasya mohitāste dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*punaḥ kapardinaṃ jaghnuḥ pāṇipādena vai dvijāḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

75-77a. Others asked him whether it was one of his Vratas and if so by whom was it demonstrated. They continued: “There are women here. How is it that this has been committed by you? Was an action like this committed by Brahmā? Or by Viṣṇu himself or by the Lord Giriśa? By whom has this evil action performed? Do not deride and deceive the Lord of Devas. You are worthy of being killed by us today.”

77b-80. On being hit and hurt by the Brāhmaṇas thus, Śaṅkara, the great holy Lord, smiled and told all those Brāhmaṇas: “Why do you hit me—a lunatic who has lost his senses? All of you are compassionate, and well-established in a friendly attitude.” Even as Lord Hara in the form of a contemptible man said this those Brāhmaṇas overwhelmed and enchanted by the Māyā of the Lord hit the matted-haired Lord with their hands and kicked him with their feet.

## \|\| 1.26.81-86 \|\|

*tāḍyamānastu tairvipraiḥ paraṃ kopamupāgamat \|*  
*tato devena te śaptā yūyaṃ vedavivarjitāḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*ūrdhvajūṭāḥ salaguḍāḥ paradāropajīvinaḥ \|*  
*ratā dyūte ca veśyāyāṃ pitṛmātṛvivarjitāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*na putre pitṛ vittaṃ ca vidyā vāpi bhaviṣyati \|*  
*śeṣo mama hato yaiśca te sarveṃdriyavarjitāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*raudrāṃ bhikṣāṃ tu bhikṣaṃtaḥ parapiṃḍopajīvinaḥ \|*  
*ātmānaṃ varṇayiṣyaṃti dhanadhānyavivarjitāḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*yaiśca tatra kṛtā viprairhanyamāne kṛpā mayi \|*  
*teṣāṃ dhanaṃ ca putrāśca dāsīdāsādayaśca vai \|\| 85 \|\|*

*kulotpannāśca vai nāryo bhaviṣyaṃti varānmama \|*  
*evaṃ śāpaṃ varaṃ dattvā gatoṃ'tardhānamīśvaraḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

81-86. On being struck by those Brāhmaṇas, he became angry. Thereupon they were cursed by the Lord: “You shall be bereft of the Vedic study. Your tuft will be tied upwards. You will be armed with sticks. You will sustain yourselves through other men’s wives. You will be addicted to the game of dice and to prostitutes. You will neglect your fathers and mothers. The wealth and learning of the father will not pass on to the son. They by whom my penis was hit shall become ineffective in all their sense-organs. They will be begging for alms in a terrific manner. They will sustain themselves through other peoples’ balls of rice. Devoid of wealth and grain, they will be muttering about themselves and their sufferings.

In the case of those who showed pity while I was being hit by the Brāhmaṇas, all of them will have wealth, sons, slaves, servants etc. With my favour, their women shall be of exalted families.” After granting the boons and cursing them Īśvara vanished.

## \|\| 1.26.87 \|\|

*tato dvijā gate deve matvā taṃ śaṃkaraṃ vibhum \|*  
*anveṣayaṃto yatnena mahākālavanaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. After the Lord had gone, they realized that it was Lord Śaṅkara. Carefully searching for him, they went to Mahākālavana.

## \|\| 1.26.88 \|\|

*snātvā sarasi rudrasya japataḥ śatarudriyam \|*  
*jāpyāvasāne tāndevo'śarīriṇyā girā'bravīt \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. After taking the holy bath in Rudrasaras, they began to utter the Śatarudriya Mantras. At the end of the Japa, the Lord told them by means of unembodied speech:

## \|\| 1.26.89-92 \|\|

*anṛtaṃ na mayā proktaṃ svaireṣvepi kutaḥ sukham \|*  
*bhūyo'pyanugrahaṃ viprā yuṣmākaṃ karavāṇyaham \|\| 89 \|\|*

*śāṃtā dāṃtāśca ye viprā bhaktimaṃto mayi sthitāḥ \|*  
*na teṣāṃ chidyate vaṃśo na dhanaṃ na ca saṃtatiḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

*agnihotraratā ye ca bhaktimaṃto janārdane \|*  
*pūjayaṃti ca brahmāṇaṃ tejorāśiṃ divākaram \|\| 91 \|\|*

*nāśubhaṃ vidyate teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ sakhye sthitā matiḥ \|*  
*etāvaduktvā deveśastūṣṇīmāsījjagatprabhuḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

89-92a. “Falsehood has not been uttered by me even wantonly. Where is the happiness therein, O Brāhmaṇas? I shall bless you further. Neither the race, nor the wealth nor the progeny becomes broken in the case of those Brāhmaṇas who are quiescent with control over the sense-organs and who remain devoted to me. Those who strictly adhere to the performance of Agnihotra, those who are devoted to Janārdana, those who worship Brahmā and Divākara (the Sun-god), the heap of refulgence, will never meet with inauspiciousness. Those whose mind is cool and equanimous will never meet with disaster.”

92b. After saying this much, the Lord, the Lord of the Devas, became silent.

## \|\| 1.26.93 \|\|

*evaṃ śāpaṃ varaṃ labdhvā devadevānmaheśvarāt \|*  
*ājagmuḥ sahitāḥ sarve yatra devaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. After obtaining the curse and the boon from Maheśvara, the Lord of Devas, all of them came to the place where Pitāmaha was present.

## \|\| 1.26.94 \|\|

*viraṃcimatha te jāpyaistoṣayanto'grataḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭastānabravīdbrahmā matto'pi vriyatāṃ varaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Propitiating Viriñci too by means of the Japas, they stayed in front of him. The pleased Brahmā told them: “May the boon be chosen and received from me too.”

## \|\| 1.26.95 \|\|

*brahmaṇastena vākyena tuṣṭāḥ sarve dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*ko varo yācyatāṃ viprāḥ parituṣṭe pitāmahe \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. All those excellent Brāhmaṇas were delighted at those words of Brahmā. They thought, ‘O Brāhmaṇas, what boon should be requested for when Pitāmaha is satisfied?’

## \|\| 1.26.96-104 \|\|

*eke tatrābruvanviprā vedānvai vṛṇavāmahai \|*  
*tato'nye ca dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ vriyatāmaviśaṃkitaiḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

*anye prāhuḥ kimasmākaṃ dhanaistuṣṭe pitāmahe \|*  
*agnihotrāṇi vedāśca śāstrāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 97 \|\|*

*śāṃtā āḍhyāśca lokāśca varadānādbhavaṃtu naḥ \|*  
*evaṃ prajalpatāṃ tatra viprāṇāṃ kopa āviśat \|\| 98 \|\|*

*parasparaṃ varārthe'tha yuddhaṃ kartuṃ samudyatāḥ \|*  
*yudhyaṃte sāyudhāḥ kecitkecittatropasarpakāḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*kecidviprā udāsīnāḥ kecidvai maunamāsthitāḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhagavānprāha viprānyuddhaṃ prakurvataḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*yasmātkumaṃtritā viprāḥ śālāyā bāhyasaṃsthite \|*  
*tasmādāmūlato viprā gulme yuddhopasarpakāḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*udāsīnastu yo gulmo vṛttihīno bhaviṣyati \|*  
*vedāstasya bhaveyurvai yastvasti maunasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

*tṛtīyaḥ sāyudho gulmo yoddhukāmastu yaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*paradāreṣu veśyāyāṃ dyūte caurye sadā rataḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*caturvidhaḥ sa vai vipro vṛttihīno bhaviṣyati \|*  
*evamuktvā yayau brahmā vairājaṃ bhavanottamam \|\| 104 \|\|*

96-104. Some of the Brāhmaṇas said: “Let us choose the Vedas.” Others said: “Let wealth and grain be requested for unhesitatingly.” Others said: “Of what avail are riches unto us, when Pitāmaha is pleased? May the Agnihotras, the Vedas, the different Śāstras, quiescent and affluent worlds belong to us through the grant of the boon.” Speaking thus, those Brāhmaṇas became indignant. For the sake (of the specification) of the boon, they attempted to fight with one another. Some of them took up arms and started fighting. Others fled from the scene. Some of the Brāhmaṇas were indifferent. Some remained silent observers.

On seeing them fighting thus, the Lord spoke to the Brāhmaṇas: “Even at. the very outskirts of the Śālā (Sacrificial Hall) the ill-advised Brāhmaṇas became angry. They began to fight and flee. The group of people who were indifferent shall become deprived of their jobs. The third group that remained tacit observers shall become learned in the Vedas. The group that took up arms and was ready to fight shall become always addicted to game of dice, prostitutes, thievery and other men’s wives. All the four types of Brāhmaṇas shall be deprived of their jobs.”

After saying this, Brahmā went to his excellent abode Vairāja.

## \|\| 1.26.105 \|\|

*evaṃ me paramaṃ kṣetraṃ munayo'vaṃtimaṃḍale \|*  
*yāṃ devanagarīṃ loke pravadantīha mānavāḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Thus, O sages, is my greatest holy spot in the zone of Avantī. Men on the earth call this a divine city.

## \|\| 1.26.106 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tu ye dvijāḥ śāṃtā vasaṃti kṣetravāsina \|*  
*na teṣāṃ durlabhaṃ kiṃcinma ma loke bhaviṣyati \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Nothing will be difficult of access in my world to those quiescent Brāhmaṇas who permanently reside in the holy spot.

## \|\| 1.26.107-109 \|\|

*kolāmukhe kurukṣetre naimiṣe puṣkareṣu ca \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ prabhāse ca tathā badarikāśrame \|\| 107 \|\|*

*gaṃgādvāre prayāge ca gaṃgāsā garasaṃgame \|*  
*rudrakoṭyāṃ virūpākṣe mitrasyāpi tathā vane \|\| 108 \|\|*

*tīrtheṣveteṣu kṣetreṣu yā siddhirdvādaśābdikā \|*  
*prāpyate mānavairloke sā māseneha labhyate \|*  
*ujjayinyāṃ na saṃdeho brahmacarye mano yadi \|\| 109 \|\|*

107-109. There are these holy Tīrthas, viz. Kolāmukha, Kurukṣetra, Naimiṣa, Puṣkara, Vārāṇasī, Prabhāsa, Badarikāśrama, Prayāga, Gaṅgādvāra, the confluence of Gaṅgā and the ocean, Rudrakoṭi, Virūpākṣa and Mitravana. The Siddhi that is achieved by men in these holy shrines in the course of twelve years, can be achieved here in Ujjayinī in a month if the mind is steadfast in celibacy. There is no doubt at all.

## \|\| 1.26.110 \|\|

*tīrthānāṃ pravaraṃ tīrthaṃ kṣetrāṇāmapi cottamam \|*  
*sadābhirucitaṃ mahyametadvai munisattamāḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. O excellent sages, this is the most excellent one of all Tīrthas: it is the most excellent holy spot. This is always pleasing to me.

## \|\| 1.26.111 \|\|

*maṃdākinyāstu māhātmyaṃ kṣetrasyotpattiruttamā \|*  
*bhūyaḥ kimanyadicchāsti śrotuṃ vai dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. The greatness of Mandākinī, the excellent origin of the holy spot (has been heard). What else do you wish to hear, O excellent Brāhmaṇas?

## \|\| 1.26.112 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*etatte brahmaṇo vākyaṃ śrutvā vyāsa tathāvidham \|*  
*vasiṣṭhādyāśca munayaḥ paraṃ dhyānamatho gatāḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:

112\. All these sages beginning with Vasiṣṭha heard this statement of Brahmā, O Vyāsa. Thereupon, they entered the greatest meditation.

## \|\| 1.26.113 \|\|

*dhyātvā tu suciraṃ kālaṃ tatra vāse mano dadhuḥ \|*  
*sāgnihotrāḥ sapatnīkā gatāścāvaṃtimaṃḍale \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. After meditating for a long time, they became inclined to live there. They went to Avantimaṇḍala along with their wives to continue their Agnihotra rites.

## \|\| 1.26.114-115 \|\|

*mahākālavanaṃ dṛṣṭvā śiprāṃ caiva mahānadīm \|*  
*śmaśānamūṣaraṃ caiva nadīṃ gandhavatīṃ tathā \|\| 114 \|\|*

*koṭitīrthamupaspṛśya cakurvāsaṃ ca tatra vai \|*  
*smṛtvā tadbrahmaṇo vākyaṃ rucisteṣāṃ tadā'bhavat \|\| 115 \|\|*

114-115. On seeing Mahākālavana, the great river Śiprā, the Śmaśāna, the Ūṣara (barren land) and the river Gandhavatī, they fixed their residence there after taking the holy bath in Koṭitīrtha. Their interest enhanced on frequently remembering the words of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.26.116 \|\|

*arundhatyā vasiṣṭhaśca gamanaṃ prati noditaḥ \|*  
*uvāca tāṃ mahātmāsau svāṃ bhāryāṃ munisattamāḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. On being urged by Arunḍhatī to go there the noble-souled Vasiṣṭha spoke to his wife, O excellent sages:

## \|\| 1.26.117-120 \|\|

*mahākālaḥ saricchiprā gatiścaiva sunirmalā \|*  
*ujjayinyāṃ viśālākṣi vāsaḥ kasya na rocate \|\| 117 \|\|*

*snānaṃ kṛtvā naro yastu mahānadyāṃ hi durlabham \|*  
*mahākālaṃ namaskṛtya naro mṛtyuṃ na śocayet \|\| 118 \|\|*

*mṛtaḥ kīṭaḥ pataṃgo vā rudra syānucaro bhavet \|*  
*yatraiṣā śrūyate muktiḥ kathaṃ sā tyajate mayā \|\| 119 \|\|*

*evaṃ prajalpyātha munipradhānastatraiva vāsaṃ sahasā cakāra \|*  
*vanasya vyuṣṭiṃ parikīrtayaṃstu sthitaḥ sahaivātra munipradhānaiḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

117-120. “O wide-eyed lady, who will not like to stay in Ujjayinī? We have Mahākāla, the river Śiprā and a goal free from impurities. A man who takes his holy bath in the great river and bows to Mahākāla who is difficult of access, will never bewail death. The dead one whether a worm, or a locust shall become a follower of Rudra. Where it is heard that salvation is obtained thus (i.e. easily), how can I forsake it.” After saying this, the chief of sages remained there itself. He stayed there with other eminent sages praising the beauty of the forest.

## Chapter 27 - The Glory of Aṅkapāda (Restoration of Sāndīpani’s Son)

## \|\| 1.27.1 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*yo'vaṃtyāmaṃkapādākhye paśyedrāmajanārdanau \|*  
*yayordarśanamātreṇa yamalokaṃ na paśyati \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:

1\. He who sees Rāma and Janārdana in the holy spot Aṅkapāda in Avantī, does not see Yamaloka as a result of their sight alone.

Vyāsa asked:

## \|\| 1.27.2 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ tāvaṃkapādākhye yātāvatra mahāmune \|*  
*na paśyedyamalokaṃ sa yadyapi brahmahā bhavet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O great sage, how did they go to the holy spot named Aṅkapāda? How is it that one who sees them does not see Yamaloka even if he were a slayer of a Brāhmaṇa?

## \|\| 1.27.3 \|\|

*sanatkumāra uvāca \|*  
*bhārāvatāraṇārthāya devau rāmajanārdanau \|*  
*avatīrṇau yadorvaṃśe divyarūpau mahādyutau \|\| 3 \|\|*

Sanatkumāra said:

3\. In order to lighten the burden (on the earth) Lord Rāma and Janārdana incarnated in the family of Yadu. They were endowed with great lustre and divine forms.

## \|\| 1.27.4-5 \|\|

*kaṃsaṃ hatvā sacāṇūramugrasenaṃ narādhipam \|*  
*abhiṣicya svayaṃ rājye yadusiṃha uvāca tam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kiṃ kāryaṃ te mayā brūhi kartavyaṃ te sute hate \|*  
*evamuktaḥ sa rājā vāṃ ugraseno'bravīdidam \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. After killing Kaṃsa along with Cāṇūra and crowning Ugrasena as the king, the lion of the family of Yadus (i.e. Kṛṣṇa) asked him, “After your son has been killed what else remains for me to do?” On being asked thus, King Ugrasena said as follows:

## \|\| 1.27.6-10 \|\|

*sarvaṃ saṃpatsyate kṛṣṇa bhavato hi na durlabham \|*  
*vijñātākhilavijñānau bhavitārāvubhāvapi \|\| 6 \|\|*

*gacchetamujjayinyāṃ vai kṛtavidyau bhaviṣyatha \|*  
*tataḥ sāṃdīpaniṃ vipraṃ jagmatū rāmakeśavau \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kaṇṭhasthāṃścakraturvedānācāramakhilaṃ ca tau \|*  
*sarahasyaṃ dhanurvedaṃ sasaṃhāraṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ahorātraiścatuḥṣaṣṭyā tadadbhutamabhūddvija \|*  
*sāṃdīpanirasaṃbhāvyaṃ tayoḥ karmātimānuṣam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*viciṃtya tau tadā mene prāptau caṃdra divākarau \|*  
*tataḥ kiṃcitsa novāca snātuṃ tīrthamathāyayau \|\| 10 \|\|*

6-10. “O Kṛṣṇa, everything will be realized (by you). Nothing is inaccessible to you. Both of you will learn all lores. Go to Ujjayinī. You will be masters of all learning.”

Then Rāma and Keśava went to Brāhmaṇa Sāndīpani. They learned by heart all the Vedas and all the Ācāras (Smṛti scriptures). They learned Dhanurveda along with the secrets and the technique of (discharging and) withdrawal. They learned all these things in the course of sixty-four days and nights. That was really a miracle, O Brāhmaṇa. Sāndīpani pondered over their superhuman and almost impossible achievement and thought that Candra (Moon) and Sūrya (Sun) had come to him. So he did not say anything. Both of them went to the Tīrtha to bathe.

## \|\| 1.27.11-14 \|\|

*śiṣyaistu sahito vipro mahākālavane'viśat \|*  
*śiṣyaiḥ saha praviṣṭau dvau tadā tau rāmakeśavau \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vandamānau mahākālaṃ sa taṃ keśavamavravīt \|*  
*tvayā nāthena devānāṃ mānuṣyatve hi tiṣṭhatā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sukhamāsīcca sādhūnāmajñānānāṃ ca sarvadā \|*  
*jane pīḍākarā ye tu sadā vā baladarpitāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yuvābhyāṃ te hatāḥ sarve kaṃsapramukhato nṛpāḥ \|*  
*munisiddhasurādīnāṃ sthitiḥ kāryā tvayā'nagha \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. The Brāhmaṇa entered Mahākālavana along with the disciples. Both of them, Rāma and Keśava too, entered along with the disciples and stood making obeisance to Mahākāla. He said to Keśava: “Since you, the Lord of Devas, incarnated as a man, good people as well as those without sense have become happy for ever. Those who had harassed the people and were always arrogant due to their strength, all those kings, the chief of whom was Kaṃsa, have been killed by both of you. Now, O sinless one, the sustenance of sages, Siddhas, Suras and others should be undertaken by you.”

## \|\| 1.27.15-21 \|\|

*kariṣyāmi tamityuktvā sa namasya tato yayau \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā sāṃdīpaniṃ śiṣyā ūcurevaṃ dinedine \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kasya na śraddadhe teṣāṃ vacastvatyadbhutaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ yayau tato draṣṭumāścaryaṃ śiṣyabhāṣitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tatastatrotthitaḥ śabdaḥ saṃśleṣe ca tathā tayoḥ \|*  
*tāvāgatau gṛhaṃ tatra gururvacanamabravīt \|\| 17 \|\|*

*na vai jñātau mayā vīrau yaduvṛṣṇikulodbhavau \|*  
*tataḥ sāṃdīpaniṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛtakṛtyo'bravīdvacaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*gurvarthaṃ kiṃ dadāmīti saha rāmeṇa harṣitaḥ \|*  
*tacchutvā vacanaṃ hṛdyaṃ guruḥ provāca harṣitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*putramicchāmyahaṃ tvatto yo mṛto lavaṇāṃbhasi \|*  
*putra eko hi me jātaḥ sa cāpi timinā hṛtaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*prabhāse tīrthayātrāyāṃ tvameva tamihānaya \|*  
*tatheti cābravītkṛṣṇo rāmasyānumate gataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

15-21. (Probably some lacuna here) “I shall do so,” saying to

## \|\| 1.27.22 \|\|

*taṃ samudra uvācedaṃ daityaḥ paṃcajano mahān \|*  
*timi rūpeṇa taṃ bālaṃ grastavānmayi saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

him thus, he bowed down and went away, looking at Sāndīpani. The disciples said this everyday. No one believed in their words (of the disciples) because it was wonderfully mysterious. Therefore he himself went (out) to see the miracle as expressed by the disciples. Then a sound arose when both of them came together. They came home. The preceptor then spoke these words: “I did not know them as the heroic scions of the family of Yadu and Vṛṣṇi.” Thereupon Kṛṣṇa who had done his duty, spoke these words to Sāndīpani in a delighted mood: Along with Balarāma, he asked, “What shall I give as the fee unto the preceptor?” On hearing those hearty words, the delighted preceptor said: “Through your effort I wish to get back my son who died in the salty sea. Only one son was born to me. He too was swallowed by a whale at Prabhāsa while I was in my pilgrimage. You do get him back.” Kṛṣṇa said, “So be it” and went away with the permission of Rāma.

22\. The Ocean told him: “Pañcajana, a great Daitya, in the form of a whale has swallowed the boy. He is staying within me.”

## \|\| 1.27.23-28 \|\|

*tataḥ paṃcajanaṃ hatvā grāharūpaṃ mahābalam \|*  
*tanmadhyasthaṃ ca jagrāha śaṃkhaṃ grasto hi yaḥ purā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*jaleśvaragṛhāttena grāheṇātīva līlayā \|*  
*tasyodare yadā bālaṃ nāptavāṃstu janārdanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yamālayagataṃ matvā tadā varuṇamabravīt \|*  
*bhagavānyādasāmīśa ratho me dīyatāṃ mahān \|\| 25 \|\|*

*purājire hatā daityā dānavā baladarpitāḥ \|*  
*mayā yena rathenādya mahyaṃ sa dīyatāṃ rathaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*nyāsabhūto ratho yaste vidhṛto nihatāriṇā \|*  
*mayā dharmaṃ puraskṛ्tya sa dīyatāmapāṃpate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yenāhave pretarājaṃ jitvā paśyāmi bālakam \|*  
*etacchrutvā prahṛṣṭātmā jñātvā kāryārthinaṃ harim \|*  
*dadau taṃ rathamakṣobhyaṃ raṇe tasmai surāsuraiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

23-28. Then he killed the excessively powerful Pañcajana who was in the form of a whale. He took out the conch from within him. Formerly this conch was taken away sportively by the whale from the house of the Lord of Waters.

When Janārḍana did not find the boy within his belly, he thought that he had gone to the abode of Yama. Then he said to Varuṇa: “O Sir, O Lord of aquatic beings, may a great chariot be given to me. Let me be given that chariot whereby Daityas and Dānavas who were haughty due to their strength were killed by me formerly in the course of a battle. After the enemies had been killed, the chariot had been kept with you as a deposit. O Lord of the Waters, let that be returned to me justly. With that chariot I can go and subdue the king of the departed ones in battle.”
